Title. Vector and Quantum Observer Geometries: Gauge Relativity and Trace Metric Bounds (GS-003)

Abstract. Scalar-valued edge defects are not comprehensive. The local defect carrier may be vector- or operator-valued, while the declared observer gauge maps its residual class to a scalar magnitude. In finite obstruction calculus, the residual class may be algebraically fixed relative to the declared repair quotient while its measured scalar magnitude depends on the observer gauge used to measure local defects. A three-edge cycle already shows the split: coordinate-channel sensing gives Φ=2 (scalar ℓ¹), while Euclidean vector-displacement sensing gives Φ=√2 (ℓ¹(E; ℓ²)). This note develops two non-scalar observer geometries — the Euclidean vector gauge and a quantum trace-distance gauge — as the worked realization of the branches Paper 001 §4.6 names but leaves undeveloped, with explicit dual-witness theory and a shared ΦΓR closure signature. All results are finite-dimensional and finite-graph.
